page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.cm4.4xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 16 physical cores of an Intel Xeon E5-2667 v4 processor running at 3.2 GHz. The instance is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying instead on network-attached storage. Network connectivity is rated at a baseline bandwidth of 6 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks indicate a moderate capability profile. The single-core CPU performance, measured via stress-ng, falls into the lower tier, while multi-core performance aligns with the average range. Memory bandwidth tests show average read speeds for both small and large blocks, though large-block write bandwidth is relatively weak. Data processing tasks, such as gzip compression and bzip3 decompression, perform at average speeds.

The instance presents a clear tradeoff between dedicated core allocation and raw single-core speed. While the dedicated Intel Xeon cores ensure consistent execution without resource contention, the older architecture limits its efficiency in modern, highly parallelized workloads like medium-scale LLM inference, which registers weak performance. From a cost-efficiency perspective, this hardware profile offers a stable, predictable resource density for legacy enterprise applications, static web serving, Redis databases, and general-purpose business logic that do not require high-speed local NVMe storage or advanced vector instructions.
